_note: Frozen content for design review. Each page is one step of the setup, the tool that does it, and the tip that saves the rework.
brief: Getting a business set up in an afternoon

slots.sub: The paperwork is the easy part and nobody tells you that. Here is the order that keeps you from redoing it.
slots.foot: Five steps, in the order they actually matter

slots.body: Sole trader, partnership or company. This decides your tax, your liability and how painful your first hire will be. It is the only choice here that is expensive to reverse.
slots.tipBody: Start with the simplest structure that covers your liability. Upgrading later is routine.

slots.body: Identity, proof of address, and the details you will retype on every form for the next decade. Doing this once in one folder is the whole trick.
slots.tipBody: Name every file so a stranger could find it. Future you is a stranger.

slots.body: A business account on day one costs nothing and saves a full weekend at tax time. Mixed personal and business spending is the single most common regret.
slots.tipBody: Open it before the first invoice, not after. Untangling six months of mixed spending is brutal.

slots.body: Bookkeeping is trivial weekly and miserable annually. The work does not grow, it just gets worse at recalling what a payment was for.
slots.tipBody: Fifteen minutes every Friday beats a lost weekend every March.

slots.body: A one-page agreement covering scope, payment terms and what happens if either side walks. Most disputes are not dishonesty, they are two people remembering differently.
slots.tipBody: One page you actually send beats ten pages you never do.

slots.body: Registration is administration. A business needs someone willing to pay you, and no amount of correct paperwork produces that first customer.
slots.tipBody: Do the setup in one afternoon, then never think about it again. Go and sell something.

slots.tagline: Nobody has ever failed because they picked the wrong company structure. Plenty have failed waiting to be certain.
